- Your organisation's own mechanism (your own locals or module).

- Managed identities with no shared keys, and logs sent to Log Analytics.

**Design from your request**
- Two App Services: the chat web app and the MCP server.
- One storage account for the uploaded documents.
- One AI Foundry account for the model.
- Everything is private, with its own virtual network and private DNS zones.
- Added because private networking and the logging defaults require them: a Log Analytics workspace and an Application Insights component.
- The chat app talks to the MCP server and to Foundry. That is the only wiring I recorded.

**Defaults I applied**
- Stages are development, test and production. You said "development stage", but a named stage doesn't replace the stack under the skill's rules. If you want only development, change `context.environments`.
- Deployment goes into existing resource groups, one group per stage, with no rights on the subscription.
- No landing zone, so the deployment builds its own network, DNS zones and workspace.
- Keys are off and the apps use managed identities.
- Only the production stage gets a larger plan (P1v3, 2 instances, zone-redundant) and ZRS storage. Development and test use B1, one instance and LRS.
- Models are processed in the EU data zone.
- Logs are kept 30 days.

- Subscription and resource group per stage (pipeline owner).
- Which pipeline system runs the deployment, and the application runtime (workload owner).
- Address ranges and subnet prefixes per stage (network team).
- How the company network reaches this network, and how company clients resolve the private DNS zones. This deployment creates those zones because no platform DNS was named.
- Which model and version to deploy, and whether Germany West Central offers it in the EU data zone (workload owner).
- Which application accesses the storage and with which role. With keys off, the account is unusable without one.
- How Application Insights connects privately.

Sign-in for the chat app defaulted to none. Company-network-only limits who can reach it, not who can sign in. Say so if you want Entra sign-in.

The resource sections list the decisions I resolved. They don't spell out every default, so some are left to resolve from the question sets at render time.
